reasons: Classification is correct: Article IV, Section I grants Licensor a unilateral option to extend the 36-month term by seven years, which is an automatic/unilateral multi-year renewal with no Customer exit right and no price cap — this fails the fallback (exit on ≤60 days' notice, uplift ≤5%) and sits in walk-away territory, so a deviation finding with a redline is warranted.

Redline is valid and targeted: it replaces only the offending Licensor-option sentence with renewal by mutual written agreement in successive 12-month periods plus a lesser-of-CPI-and-3% uplift cap, which is exactly the rule's preferred position and its stated redline guidance (12-month renewal term, capped uplift). Surrounding termination language and subsections II/III are left intact.

Failed deterministic checks are not substantive: the 'notice window ≤60 days' regex finds no number because the preferred position chosen here (mutual written agreement) has no non-renewal notice window, and the changed-character ratio reflects a rule-mandated sentence replacement rather than an over-broad rewrite.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, correctly cites the playbook position, and notes the internal consistency with subsections II and III.
